subject: Short-term reserved capacity for BrightMart holiday sale — taper and exception flow
body:
From: Nina Patel <ops@brightmart.com>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.com
Cc: Samir Gupta <procurement@brightmart.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: short-term reserved capacity for holiday promotion

Hi Camila,

We have a high-traffic promotion planned for the US storefront on Sep 2–6. Our infra team expects a sustained increase in inference QPS for the Redwood-powered checkout assistant. Can Redwood provide a short-term reserved slice (dedicated GPUs) and a temporary autoscale-exception window to avoid throttling?

Preliminary estimates:
- Peak concurrency: ~1.2k open sessions/minute
- Token rate: ~1.8M tokens/hour during peak windows
- Latency requirement: p95 < 120ms

We are asking for a 5-day reserved window with a 24h warmup and 24h taper afterwards. Please advise what info you need for sizing and procurement.

Thanks,
Nina
Nina Patel
Head of Ops — BrightMart
ops@brightmart.com

---
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Nina Patel <ops@brightmart.com>
Cc: Samir Gupta <procurement@brightmart.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: short-term reserved capacity for holiday promotion

Hi Nina — thanks for the details. We can support a short-term carve for that window but need to coordinate a few internal items before committing:

Action items I need from BrightMart (quick):
- Confirm expected sustained QPS and 1-hour peak multiplier (if you have a p95->p999 multiplier used for safety).
- Confirm model(s) in use and max sequence lengths (so we can finalize GPU selection).
- Specify whether you need KV/response caching to be pre-populated during warmup.

What we will do on our side:
- Share a sizing proposal and cost estimate (attachment: reservation_matrix_v2.xlsx).
- Propose an autoscale-exception flow: explicit ramp-up (24h), reserved steady window (5 days), 24h taper, and a fallback policy that routes to a smaller hosted variant if we hit unexpected capacity pressure.
- Draft an amendment to your MSA for the carve (SLA implications noted — see SLA_change_redlines.pdf).

Cc-ing Product (Kimberly) and Infra (Marcus) to confirm feasibility and the recommended taper policy. Laura — can you advise on runbook ownership and on-call alerting during the window? Dev — I’ll need a pricing hold to share with procurement.

Attached: reservation_matrix_v2.xlsx (size scenarios).

Best,
Camila Reyes
Senior Customer Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.com

---
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com, Nina Patel <ops@brightmart.com>, Samir Gupta <procurement@brightmart.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: short-term reserved capacity for holiday promotion

Camila — thanks for looping us in. A few product constraints and proposals:

1) Autoscale-exception constraints
- We can enable a temporary override of the autoscale governor for a named slate, but it must be time-boxed and require a manual rollback trigger.
- The override will allow higher headroom but will not change model-level memory limits; we may choose a different quantized variant for cost/liveness tradeoffs.

2) Taper plan (recommended)
- Warmup (24h): provision reserved CPUs/GPUs, run a scripted load to pre-populate KV cache.
- Steady (5d): reserved capacity active; monitoring at token-level and per-token cost breakdown visible in Console.
- Taper (24h): reduce reservations by 50% for first 12h, then to 10% for next 12h, then release.
- Fallback: automatic routing to a 7B hosted-optimized variant if latency degrades beyond p95 150ms for 10 consecutive minutes.

3) Open questions for procurement/legal:
- Are you able to accept a temporary SLA carve that excludes contiguous availability guarantees for the taper window? (We have suggested redlines in SLA_change_redlines.pdf.)
- Billing: will BrightMart accept prorated committed capacity pricing with a short-term uplift?

If procurement confirms the billing path, Infra can lock in the slice.

-Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Director, Product — Redwood Inference

---
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com, Nina Patel <ops@brightmart.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: short-term reserved capacity for holiday promotion

All — feasibility check from Infra side. Short summary: feasible with the following technical approach.

Sizing assumptions (based on BrightMart numbers):
- We'll provision a 16-GPU slate (A100-equivalent) for the steady window. This maps to an estimated sustained throughput of ~1.5k QPS for the chosen quantized 13B variant with batch optimizations.
- Warmup: run KV pre-population and warm-cache synthetic traffic to reach expected cache hit rate by hour 20.

Autoscale-exception implementation notes:
- Create a temporary reservation object scoped to BrightMart account -> slate-BRM-3321-temp.
- Apply autoscale override that increases max_batch_size and extends request-queue depth during the window.
- Implement automated telemetry to hit the fallback routing rules if CPU/GPU utilization crosses 85% for >10m.

Operational runbook links: https://runbook.redwood.com/BRM-3321-temp-slate-runbook (internal)

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: contiguous network events or AZ-level issues. Mitigation: cross-AZ placement + immediate fallback to hosted variant.
- Risk: uplifted tail latency if token sizes spike. Mitigation: pre-warm with a synthetic mix, and enable kv-prefix caching for common queries.

Next steps from Infra: once procurement signs off, Infra will allocate the slate and schedule warmup. Laura — can you own the runbook during the steady window and evict lower-priority queued work if we hit contention?

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Infrastructure Engineer — Redwood Inference
